notes: A CORRECTION, NOT A NEW ADJUDICATION. bmdb 1553 (library-ruling consistency pass), sqlite, b5. EXPORT SURFACE: libsqlite3 is built and installed (main.mk:1599-1608, install-lib/install-dll), and ext/ sources are compiled into it or built as documented loadable extensions (ext/misc/README.md); SQLITE_PRIVATE makes internal functions static only in the amalgamation build, and the separate-source build also compiles (ADR-0010). Every non-static function in these sources therefore has an open caller set (ADR-0011 742a1571, 6b28c8d7), and in-tree call sites prove nothing about a value arriving through its parameters. SELECTION: existing FP labels on non-static functions in exported sources whose recorded reason is caller-side (callers, call sites, contract, precondition, "always valid/never NULL"); tool-only files with their own main() excluded. METHOD: each row read at source by a reviewer; FP -> TP only where the verdict rested solely on callers for a parameter-derived value. Rows with a real in-function basis (a guard present in every build, a null-tolerant callee, a misfire, a value not from a parameter, a language guarantee) or where the keyword match was noise keep FP. assert/DEBUGASSERT/NEVER()/ALWAYS() are not guards (each compiles out or constant-folds in a compilable build). A fresh-context refuter re-checked a random sample of flips and stands. RESULT: 12 rows reviewed, 12 flip FP -> TP here, 0 keep FP. RULINGS APPLIED IN THIS BATCH (Brandon, 2026-09-25): (1) address-of is strict: &p->field and &p->a[i] evaluate p->field, undefined for a null p (C11 6.5.2.3; 6.5.3.2 exempts only &*E and &E[i]), so a key line forming &p->f with p an unproven parameter is TP; plain f(p) into a project function stays FP under aurora-lint 4bbf15d1. (2) a (pointer, length) parameter pair is a caller contract, not a basis: TP unless every call site provably validates the length, which needs a closed caller set. Rows re-checked under these rulings from earlier 1553 batches are included here. Counting basis: distinct (project, commit, file, line, rule) keys. No precision claim is made here.
